text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines a retrieval component with a language model. The retriever selects external evidence relevant to a user query, and the generator uses that evidence to formulate an answer. The retrieval corpus can be a collection of documents, web pages, or enterprise records.
title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Overview

text: A typical RAG pipeline first converts documents into chunks and embeddings, stores them in a searchable index, retrieves candidate passages for a query, and supplies selected passages to a generator. Hybrid retrieval can combine lexical matching such as BM25 with semantic vector retrieval.
title: RAG Retrieval and Generation

text: Trust-aware RAG does not treat every retrieved passage as equally reliable. A trust score can combine query relevance, source reliability, agreement with other evidence, support for the claim, and estimated poisoning risk. Low-trust evidence can be down-ranked or quarantined.
title: Evidence Trust in RAG

text: Knowledge poisoning occurs when malicious or misleading content is inserted into a retrieval corpus so that a RAG system retrieves the manipulated evidence. A successful defense should detect suspicious evidence and avoid grounding an answer in it.
title: Knowledge Poisoning

text: A self-healing RAG workflow can quarantine suspicious passages, re-retrieve alternatives, verify the replacement evidence, and regenerate the answer. The system should expose uncertainty or abstain when adequate verified evidence is unavailable.
title: Self-Healing Retrieval
